facts: CSA research note (2026-09-22): Heapjack (Codex Desktop, shared V8 heap -> validation token read -> unsandboxed command exec even in read-only mode) fixed in Desktop build 26.818.21641; Overpatch (Codex CLI, apply_patch + symlink widening workspace-write to full filesystem write / persistence) fixed in CLI 0.149.0. No CVE; OpenAI gave only an informal spokesperson confirmation ('we addressed both issues in August').

CSA defender recommendations: 'Confirm that all Codex Desktop installations are running build 26.818.21641 or later and that all Codex CLI installations are running version 0.149.0 or later; treat any earlier version as vulnerable'; 'Run coding agents that process untrusted repository content inside an additional layer of host-level isolation, such as a disposable virtual machine or container with no access to production credentials'; audit for unexpected open/launchd activity; check .zshrc/.bashrc for appended commands; flag patches that reference paths outside the project, including symlinks and /tmp.

Codex rust-v0.149.0 release notes list security-relevant changes without advisory wording: #39614 'Prevent apply_patch from widening write permissions', #39205 'Reject symbolic links in memory workspaces', #39653 'Enforce filesystem permissions when loading AGENTS.md', #39623 'Prevent protected-path rename bypasses in macOS Seatbelt', #39659 'Harden unsandboxed patch filesystem access', #39083 'Harden Windows sandbox provisioning against reparse points', and Linux sandbox capability drop / Bubblewrap IPC isolation. WebFetch reported the release date as 'August 20, 2024'; the item record has observed_at 2026-08-20 and the CSA note says August 2026, so 2024 is taken as a parsing error.

Claude Code official managed-settings docs (code.claude.com/docs/en/managed-settings): requiredMinimumVersion 'blocks an outdated binary from starting and doesn't end a session that's already running'; it applies at the next session start; 'requiredMinimumVersion and requiredMaximumVersion fail open by design: an invalid value is dropped rather than enforced'.

Codex managed requirements.toml (cloud-managed, MDM, or /etc/codex/requirements.toml) can lock allowed_sandbox_modes and approval policies. A third-party guide (codex.danielvaughan.com, 2026-07-16) says it does not enforce a minimum CLI version itself, and recommends a version-floor check in CI or the launcher. Not confirmed against official OpenAI docs.

Existing RMD-I16-001 (official, last_verified 2026-08-15) already covers version tracking, advisory monitoring, a CVE version floor, and devcontainer isolation, but its monitoring trigger is advisory/CVE-based.

Related remedy RMD-SYMLINKTOCTOU-001 (official, 2026-09-28) already lists Codex CLI 0.151.0 for symlink-class fixes and OS-layer denyRead/denyWrite as a second layer; it overlaps with the Overpatch class.
inferences: The remedy mechanism (pin and update versions, monitor the vendor, add isolation layers) is unchanged. The new aspect is that advisory/CVE-only monitoring misses silent fixes. RMD-I16-001 therefore needs an update, not a new remedy ID.

Without a CVE, users cannot map exposure to a version. The practical answer is to watch release notes and changelogs as security sources, and to raise the minimum version whenever an unlabeled sandbox or permission hardening fix appears.
The sandbox should be recorded as one layer, not the boundary: a disposable VM or container with no production credentials is the independent second layer CSA recommends.
RMD-I07-001 (Skill/Plugin/MCP audit) and RMD-I10-001 (CI workflow hardening plus agent version pin) stay valid as adjacent remedies and do not need updates for this change.
